question: What is the main goal of using quality improvement metrics in nursing care?

options.B: To track the impact of care changes
options.C: To punish staff for poor charting
options.D: To replace daily nursing shift reports

explanation: Metrics give teams the feedback needed to see if a nursing intervention is actually working. [learn more](GST319_U3_T2#GST319_U3_T2_h1)

question: How does quality improvement measurement differ from traditional clinical research?

options.A: It ignores patient safety outcomes entirely
options.B: It uses small, rapid tests in real clinical settings
options.C: It requires large double-blind patient trials
options.D: It focuses solely on hospital financial budgets

explanation: Improvement work happens fast in daily practice to test ideas, rather than waiting years for formal research trials. [learn more](GST319_U3_T2#GST319_U3_T2_h1)

question: Which measure tracks the final clinical result or the voice of the patient?
explanation: Outcome measures tell you the ultimate result of the care provided to the patient. [learn more](GST319_U3_T2#GST319_U3_T2_h2)

question: A ward manager tracks staff fatigue levels while implementing a new hourly rounding schedule. What type of measure is staff fatigue?
explanation: Balancing measures check for side effects or unintended problems in other parts of the system when a change is made. [learn more](GST319_U3_T2#GST319_U3_T2_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of an operational definition in data collection?

options.A: To increase the speed of patient discharge
options.B: To remove ambiguity in how data is counted
options.C: To evaluate nursing staff performance scores
options.D: To reduce the cost of hospital equipment

explanation: Clear definitions ensure everyone measures the exact same thing every single time. [learn more](GST319_U3_T2#GST319_U3_T2_h3)

question: What happens if a ward fails to establish a clear data collection plan?

options.B: Different staff may count events inconsistently
options.C: Doctors take over all nursing data duties

explanation: Without a standardized plan, individual interpretation leads to unreliable and messy data. [learn more](GST319_U3_T2#GST319_U3_T2_h3)

question: What is the horizontal reference line that splits a run chart into two equal halves called?
explanation: The median splits the data points so that half are above and half are below the line. [learn more](GST319_U3_T2#GST319_U3_T2_h4)

question: How do nurses use a run chart during a quality improvement project?

options.A: To replace the official patient bed register
options.B: To separate normal variation from real system improvement
options.C: To punish staff who miss documentation targets
options.D: To calculate annual hospital financial profits

explanation: Run charts help teams see if changes lead to real improvement rather than just random up-and-down daily noise. [learn more](GST319_U3_T2#GST319_U3_T2_h4)

question: What action should a team take when a test of change shows clear, sustained improvement?

options.A: Ignore the data and restart the project
options.B: Adopt the change into routine practice
options.D: Punish staff who did not participate

explanation: Proven successful interventions should be permanently integrated into daily clinical workflows. [learn more](GST319_U3_T2#GST319_U3_T2_h5)

question: Why is reacting to every single up-and-down data point a mistake in quality improvement?

options.A: It stops doctors from writing prescriptions
options.B: It reduces the total number of hospital beds
options.C: It ignores normal day-to-day system variation
options.D: It breaks hospital computer networking systems

explanation: Overreacting to random daily noise leads to constant, confusing changes in nursing procedures. [learn more](GST319_U3_T2#GST319_U3_T2_h5)
